articles.title: How to log Outlook and Teams meetings to Jira as worklogs
articles.excerpt: Someone asked Atlassian Community in 2019 how to log time from an Outlook calendar appointment to Jira. People are still asking in 2025, on the Toggl forum too, and the answers have not improved much:…
articles.body: Someone asked Atlassian Community in 2019 how to log time from an Outlook calendar appointment to Jira. People are still asking in 2025, on the Toggl forum too, and the answers have not improved much: a Tempo link, an Outlook add-in that has since disappeared, and "create a Meetings ticket". The confusion starts with the word "integration". Atlassian's own Outlook add-in is about issues and email: create an issue from a message, see issue details in the sidebar. It does not log time. Most "Jira Outlook calendar" results are about getting Jira due dates and sprints into Outlook, again the wrong direction. What the question means is: I have an Outlook calendar full of Teams meetings, my hours live in Jira worklogs, how do I get one into the other.

articles.title: November 24 is a deadline if your agent touches money
articles.excerpt: Most of this week's bank-versus-agent argument is abstract. One part of it is not. Wells Fargo's updated online access agreement takes effect November 24, and it treats instructions from an agent you…
articles.body: Most of this week's bank-versus-agent argument is abstract. One part of it is not. Wells Fargo's updated online access agreement takes effect November 24, and it treats instructions from an agent you gave your login to as your own actions, including actions beyond the authority you meant to give. Other banks are writing similar language. If you ship agents, that date is a deadline, and here is what it actually demands. Your threat model just changed. The risk is no longer only that an agent does something wrong. It is that everything it does on shared credentials is attributed to your user, legally, with no separate record under the agent's name.

articles.body: Cutting a 90-minute podcast into clips by hand takes ages. That's the job the Shorts Generator in ClapClip AI is for. I'm Chris, I build it, and here's what it does and, just as important, what it sends where. What it does Give it a long video: a podcast, interview, stream or webinar. ClapClip transcribes the speech, scores each stretch for hook, flow, value and trend, and returns a ranked shortlist of clip candidates. You preview them and export the ones you want, as 9:16, 1:1 or 16:9 clips with burned-in captions. It also suggests captions and hashtags for posting. Where the data goes Transcription and rendering run on your Windows PC, so the video itself isn't uploaded. The clip-selection step sends the transcript text to an AI service.

articles.title: My Mac app's build fails if it links networking code
articles.excerpt: Stillroom is an encrypted vault for the Mac. It keeps files, notes, passwords and two-factor codes, and it never goes online: no account, no server, no sync, no update check, no analytics. Writing "we…
articles.body: Stillroom is an encrypted vault for the Mac. It keeps files, notes, passwords and two-factor codes, and it never goes online: no account, no server, no sync, no update check, no analytics. Writing "we never connect to the internet" on a website is easy. Keeping it true is harder, because one dependency, one convenience call or one well-meant "check for updates" is enough to break it, and nobody notices until someone runs Little Snitch. So the claim is checked by the build. If the app binary can reach the network, the build fails and there is nothing to ship.

articles.body: The original Fable checked all of the boxes of a good fairy tale: a classic good-versus-evil tale set in a high-fantasy version of Fake Britain. You played as a hero (literally, the “Hero of Oakvale”) fighting against a guy who considered burning down villages his idea of a good time. Fable ’s big innovation lay in its morality system: Depending on your actions, the hero’s appearance would change (ex: you’d grow devil horns if you were evil), as would the way the citizens of Albion would react to him. Just like the main characters of stories like Jack and the Beanstalk , Little Red Riding Hood , and other quintessential fairy tales, you were consigned to live with the consequences of your actions — good or bad.

articles.excerpt: Satellites are watching fireballs blaze through Earth's atmosphere, strengthening planetary defense knowhow and helping scientists learn more about space debris impacts.
articles.body: It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 1, 1962: The Soviet Union Launches Mars 1 spacecraft to Red Planet during the Space Race
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. While it did end up flying by Mars , the mission was not exactly a success. After it separated from the rocket, it deployed its solar panels and started cruising toward Mars. When mission controllers were checking out the telemetry it transmitted back to Earth, they found out that Mars 1 had sprung a leak in one of the gas valves that controls the spacecraft's orientation. And without a working orientation system, Mars 1 would have a hard time pointing its antennas in the right direction. It lost contact with Earth when it was about halfway to Mars . A model of Mars 1, a Mars flyby spacecraft launched to the Red Planet by the Soviet Union on Nov. 1, 1962.

Telescopically, the southern side of its famous ring system is currently tilted about 6½ degrees to our line of sight. articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
